text: noelle: Customer report: deep link to /guides/streams#json/ndjson-examples doesn't jump to the examples section. It just lands at the top of the page. Report from support: https://docs.redwood.ai/guides/streams#json/ndjson-examples ben: that path fragment with a slash looks suspicious. some slugifiers encode `/` as `%2F` in the generated id. can you paste the heading from the page? noelle: page snippet: ```md ### JSON/NDJSON examples Small examples showing ndjson vs json streams. ``` tara: yep. our site (docusaurus build) generates an id like `json%2Fndjson-examples` because of the slash in the heading. external links used a plain `/` or a hyphen variant. browsers will only jump to exact id. linkcheck previously passed because it compares rendered anchors to links but doesn't decode percent-encoded chars consistently. ben: ok quick options: 1) change the heading to `JSON & NDJSON examples` or `JSON \u002F NDJSON examples`? 2) add explicit id `{#json-ndjson-examples}` and update any inbound links. I prefer explicit ids for stable deep links. noelle: i'll open a PR that 1) changes heading to `JSON & NDJSON examples {#json-ndjson-examples}` 2) adds a small CI check that flags percent-encoded sequences in generated ids (e.g., `%2F`, `%20`, etc.) and reports candidate headings. link-bot: New PR #3891 by @noelle: "fix slash-encoded heading ids + linkcheck enhancement" ci-bot: Running `yarn docs:linkcheck` for PR #3891 and `mkdocs build --strict`. Additional step: `grep -oP 'id=\"[^\"]+\"' .site/**/*.html | sed 's/id=\"//;s/\"//' | grep -P '%[0-9A-Fa-f]{2}' || true` to surface encoded ids. ci-bot: Linkcheck output: found encoded id `json%2Fndjson-examples` in guides/streams.html. Also found existing external links pointing to both `#json/ndjson-examples` and `#json-ndjson-examples` (mixed). Failing the job to avoid silently mismatched anchors. ben: can you update the PR to 1) add explicit `{#json-ndjson-examples}` and 2) create a brief redirect note in the page for old links? maybe a short HTML anchor `` before the heading to handle legacy links? but that re-introduces raw HTML ids which we try to avoid. tara: i'd avoid adding raw HTML ids. instead add a small snippet in the CI that generates a mapping of percent-encoded ids -> normalized ids and optionally create a tiny `legacy-anchors.yml` we can use to add client-side JS redirects if we want. but easiest is add explicit id and add a short section in the docs migration notes to update external links. noelle: updated PR: changed heading and added explicit id. Removed any HTML hacks. Also extended linkcheck rule to fail PRs that introduce new percent-encoded ids and to print a helpful message with suggested explicit id. Patch excerpt: ```diff -### JSON/NDJSON examples +### JSON & NDJSON examples {#json-ndjson-examples} ``` ci-bot: Re-running checks: encoded id count is 0 on changed pages. Linkcheck passes for PR #3891. link-bot: Reviewers requested: @ben, @tara. ben: LGTM. Merged commit e5b7a6c. Thanks for the thorough CI message 1. noelle: closing loop with support and the customer. They confirmed the deep link now lands correctly when using `#json-ndjson-examples`. Also filed a follow-up to scan the repo for other headings containing slashes and percent-encoded sequences. tara: I'll add a line to CONTRIBUTING: "Avoid literal slashes in heading text; prefer ampersand, 'vs', or explicit heading ids for stable anchors." noelle: if you see any odd deep links, drop them here. thanks! :sparkles:
